newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr closes on highs on samurai-linked demand.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr closes on highs on samurai-linked demand.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed strongly on Thursday, underpinned by strong samurai-linked demand, and dealers said it looked set to threaten new eight-year highs.
The Kiwi finished the session at US$0.7017/24 and 66.83 on its Trade-Weighted Index, up from 0.6989/96 and 66.57 at the opening.
"The global markets still have a demand for Kiwi, still driven by yield, and the yield is very much the focus at the moment," said a Wellington dealer, who predicted a 0.7010-30 range overnight.
Phil Lindberg at Bankers Trust said the currency was still looking very well bid and set to take another crack at the topside. Offshore players would be looking for any dips.

"The base is moving higher as we take out new levels and I think that, coupled with the fact there's still obvious samurai and euro issuing interest out there, means it's hard to really see the Kiwi coming off a long way," he said.
The currency traded a 0.6987-7019 range on the day.

Lindberg said June quarter GDP data due on Friday were unlikely to move the market much unless way out of line with consensus forecasts, which are for a 0.4 percent quarterly rise in production-based GDP.
Dealers said after a quiet start to the day, strong buying interest out of Asia had caught the market short and stop-loss buy orders had been triggered just above 70 U.S. cents.
The currency has shrugged off uncertainty over the outcome of the October 12 general election, reaching 0.7027 last week in the latest of a series of eight-year highs.
